question:
The two circles pictured have the same center \(C.\) Chord \(\overline{AD}\) is tangent to the inner circle at \(B,\) \(AC\) is \(10,\) and chord \(\overline{AD}\) has length \(16.\) What is the area between the two circles?

[Figure 1](figures/2010_AMC_8_Q19_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Circle areas depend on the squares of their radii, so we only need to find \(CB^2\) before subtracting the areas.

[Figure 1](figures/2010_AMC_8_Q19_question_fig1.svg)

The right-angle marker at \(B\) makes \(ABC\) and \(DBC\) right triangles. Also, \(CA=CD=10\), since both are radii of the outer circle. Applying the Pythagorean theorem to these two triangles gives
\[
AB^2=10^2-CB^2=BD^2.
\]
Because lengths are nonnegative, \(AB=BD\). Their sum is \(AD=16\), so \(AB=BD=8\).

Now triangle \(ABC\) gives the squared inner radius:
\[
CB^2=10^2-8^2=100-64=36.
\]
The area between the circles is the outer circle's area minus the inner circle's area:
\[
\pi AC^2-\pi CB^2
=100\pi-36\pi
=64\pi.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{64\pi}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
